title: Stars brewing in N159
caption: The star-forming region N159 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: N159, LHA 120-N 159, Papillon Nebula · Large Magellanic Cloud · constellation Dorado · about 161,000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, E. Sabbi, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb); Acknowledgement: M. H. Özsaraç

recognition.text: ESA/Webb Picture of the Month, October 2026 (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Smoky orange clouds, pale blue bubbles and dark red filaments fill this Webb view of N159, a turbulent star-forming region about 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy that orbits our own. At under three million years old, it is one of the youngest star-forming regions there.

Cold clouds of molecular hydrogen are collapsing under gravity to make stars, and many of the newborns are massive and hot. Their ultraviolet light energizes the gas around them, which glows in the pale blue patches, while their winds carve ridges and hollow out cavities. The orange comes from carbon-based molecules. The dark red filaments are cool molecular hydrogen, the densest part of the nebula, which for now shields the newest stars from the harsh light around them.
Zoom in and stars appear inside those filaments and inside orange pillars reaching into the blue bubbles. The bright spot on the left is the Papillon Nebula, a compact knot of glowing hydrogen.
scale: The frame spans roughly 230 light-years, according to the release. Its light set out about 161,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam in ten near-infrared filters, from 1.15 to 4.7 microns. Shorter wavelengths are shown in blue and cyan, glowing molecular hydrogen in green, carbon-based molecules in orange and the longest wavelengths in red.
understand.eye: All of this is near-infrared light, which the eye can’t see, so every color here is assigned.

explore: Webb found very faint stars here, under a tenth of the Sun’s mass, and could tell fully formed stars apart from young ones still wrapped in their birth clouds. The western part holds more of these young objects, packed more tightly, which suggests it is at an earlier stage of collapse.
alt: Thick orange clouds and dark red filaments around pale blue cavities of glowing gas, scattered with bright stars, and a bright compact spot at left.
